title: Write a parser
prompt: Implement parse_duration(text) in durations.py. It turns a duration into seconds: '1h30m' is 5400, '45s' is 45, '2h' is 7200, '1h2m3s' is 3723. Spaces are allowed between the parts and around the whole duration ('1h 30m' and ' 3m ' are fine). Hours, minutes and seconds each appear at most once and in that order, and a part may be any size ('90m' is 5400). Anything else (an empty or blank string, a bare number like '10', an unknown unit like '5x', a repeated unit like '1h1h', a negative number, a decimal like '1.5h') raises ValueError.
